name: New Hampshire White Mountains
agency: USFS White Mountain National Forest, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
summary: Alpine ridgelines, glacially carved ravines, waterfalls, and AMC high huts from Franconia Ridge across the Presidential Range to the Wildcats, Carters and Baldfaces at the Maine border.

trails.name: Falling Waters Trail to Little Haystack
trails.condition_note: Waterfalls flowing well; wet granite slabs near Cloudland Falls.
trails.description: Ascends alongside Stairs, Swiftwater, and 80-ft Cloudland Falls to emerge above treeline on Little Haystack Mountain.

trails.name: Franconia Ridge Trail (Little Haystack – Mt. Lincoln – Mt. Lafayette)
trails.condition_note: Exposed alpine knife-edge ridge above 1,450 m; high winds and rapid fog possible.
trails.description: Iconic 360-degree alpine traverse along the Appalachian Trail linking Little Haystack (4,780 ft), Mt. Lincoln (5,089 ft), and Mt. Lafayette (5,249 ft).

trails.name: Greenleaf Trail & Old Bridle Path Descent
trails.condition_note: Potable water and shelter at AMC Greenleaf Hut; rocky ledges on Agony Ridge.
trails.description: Descends from Mt. Lafayette past AMC Greenleaf Hut and down Old Bridle Path with sweeping views back across Franconia Ridge.

trails.name: Franconia Ridge Complete Loop (Falling Waters, Ridge & Old Bridle Path)
trails.condition_note: Premier White Mountains loop; carry wind shell for alpine zone.
trails.description: New Hampshire's signature 8.9-mile alpine loop climbing Falling Waters Trail, traversing Franconia Ridge over three 4,000-footers, and descending via Greenleaf Hut and Old Bridle Path.

trails.name: Lonesome Lake & Cannon Balls View Loop
trails.condition_note: Bog bridges around Lonesome Lake in great shape; family & dog friendly.
trails.description: Steady woodland climb from Lafayette Place to glacial Lonesome Lake and AMC Lonesome Lake Hut with dramatic reflections of Franconia Ridge.

trails.name: Mt. Washington via Tuckerman Ravine Trail
trails.condition_note: Lingering snow/ice patches in Tuckerman headwall; steep boulder talus on summit cone.
trails.description: Classic steep ascent from Pinkham Notch Visitor Center through glacial Tuckerman Ravine bowl and up the boulder-strewn summit cone to the 6,288-ft rooftop of New England.

trails.name: Mt. Washington Loop via Lion Head & Boott Spur
trails.condition_note: Long exposure above treeline across Lion Head, Mt. Washington, Lakes of the Clouds, and Boott Spur.
trails.description: Grand Presidential Range loop ascending Lion Head ridge to Mt. Washington summit, visiting AMC Lakes of the Clouds Hut on Crawford Path, and descending scenic Boott Spur.
